one_liner: SSSE3 lookup-table UTF-8/UTF-16/UTF-32 transcoder, 7-13x faster than its own Hoehrmann-DFA scalar path on BMP-heavy text.
what_it_does: Converts UTF-8 to UTF-16LE or UTF-32LE and back on x86, with full validation by default (overlongs, surrogates, values above U+10FFFF rejected). You build a processor from ProcessorSelector<Src, Dst>::WithOptions<Mode, MaxBytes, SpeedMult> and then call message-level routines (ConvertInMemory, ConvertFile), lower-level buffer routines, or a shared library that exports iconv_open/iconv/iconv_close with documented deviations from the iconv spec. It is not a drop-in for ICU or std::codecvt: the API is its own, and the author calls the project mainly a proof of concept.
how_it_is_fast: Decode takes the movemask of continuation bytes in a 16-byte SSSE3 register (15 bits after dropping bit 0) and uses it to index a 32768-entry table (10609 reachable entries) holding pshufb masks, the bytes consumed and the code units produced; pshufb + pmaddubsw then assemble up to 8 UTF-16 code units per step, and validation compares header bits, overlong minimums and the surrogate range against per-entry masks. Encode uses a 256-entry table indexed by a code-unit length mask. Anything the fast path cannot handle (non-BMP characters, invalid bytes) drops to Bjoern Hoehrmann's DFA decoder or a branchy scalar encoder for that 16-byte block. The benchmarked configuration (SpeedMult = 4) decodes 4 interleaved streams over quarters of the buffer to hide latency, then copies the 4 outputs into one buffer, and unrolls the encoder 4x.
when_to_use: Bulk conversion of large buffers (hundreds of KB and up) of BMP text dominated by 2- and 3-byte characters (Cyrillic, Greek, CJK) on x86 with SSSE3
Validating UTF-8 to UTF-16 conversion at roughly 1-1.7 cycles per input byte (README, Ryzen 1600) where a scalar converter's 5-15 cycles per byte is the bottleneck
Studying or borrowing the movemask-indexed pshufb lookup-table technique; core/DecoderProcess.h and core/EncoderProcess.h are compact and BSL-1.0
Projects that need an iconv-shaped C API for UTF-8 to and from UTF-16LE/UTF-32LE only and can live with its documented deviations
when_not_to_use: ASCII-heavy or Latin-script text: there is no ASCII shortcut in the default 3-byte mode (each step emits at most 8 characters per 16-byte load), and Lemire and Mula's paper reports u8u16 and utf8sse4 beating it on English, French, German and other European-language files, utf8sse4 sometimes by 2x (search snippet only, paper blocked here)

Text with many supplementary-plane characters (emoji, historic scripts): non-BMP code points always take the scalar slow path, and the README says over 99% of characters must stay on the fast path for good speed
ARM, other non-x86 targets, or code that must use AVX2/AVX-512: SSSE3 only, no runtime dispatch, no portable fallback build
Short strings: inputs under 16 bytes run entirely on the scalar path, and the 4-stream decoder only engages from 128 bytes; the first call also pays for building the 2 MiB lookup table
Production code that needs maintenance: last commit 2020-04-19, no releases, no issues ever filed, one unmerged typo PR from 2022

integration.form: source-drop (add src/ to the include path and compile the core, buffer and message .cpp files; optional iconv shared library)
integration.dependencies: none (SSE2/SSSE3 intrinsics; scalar decoder embeds Hoehrmann's MIT-licensed DFA table)
integration.min_toolchain: C++11 with -mssse3 on GCC/Clang/MinGW; MSVC build scripts use cl /O2 /Oi (version not documented); CMake 3.2.1 for tests and samples
integration.platforms: x86 and x86-64 with SSSE3 required; Windows and Linux build scripts
integration.thread_safety: Not documented. One processor object per thread (processors hold buffers and state). The decoder and encoder LUT singletons are built lazily on first use with no synchronization, and the pointer is published before the table is filled, so warm them up from one thread before converting in parallel.
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — the iconv shared library mimics iconv for UTF-8 to and from UTF-16LE/UTF-32LE only, returns 1 instead of a character count, and may stop with E2BIG while up to about 64 KB of input remain unless the output buffer is sized with its extension call; the C++ API is its own

gotchas: The README table used FileConverter's default SpeedMult = 4 (4-stream decoder, 4x-unrolled encoder), but ProcessorSelector<...>::WithOptions<> and the README usage example default to SpeedMult = 1; pass SpeedMult = 4 explicitly to get the measured configuration (the multi-stream processor does not support error correction).

Benchmark normalisation: the core rdtsc timer divides by input bytes, so encode cells are cycles per UTF-16 byte, not per UTF-8 byte as the README says; for the random set the two sizes match, but for the fb2 file (Cyrillic plus ASCII XML markup) encode and decode cells are not directly comparable, and rdtsc counts TSC reference ticks rather than core cycles. Both rows share the normalisation, so the fast-vs-scalar ratios stand.

The README numbers date from 2018 (readme.md added 2018-04-09, never re-measured); the 4-stream decoder was changed on 2019-07-27 to keep multistreaming past supplementary characters, and that code reads the uninitialised ok1..ok3 flags if stream 0 fails on its first 16-byte block (undefined behaviour, normally harmless because the scalar fallback still decodes correctly).

cmFast and cmFull skip validation, so invalid UTF-8 (or a non-BMP character in cmFast) is undefined behaviour; keep the default cmValidate for untrusted input. The validating decoder LUT is 32768 x 64 bytes = 2 MiB (1 MiB without validation), allocated with _mm_malloc on first use and never freed, and it competes for L2/L3 with the rest of the program.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Among the catalogued converters, encoding_rs (C API via encoding_c) has ASCII fast paths and is about 7x ICU on English UTF-8/UTF-16, and xutf and Parabix are measured against simdutf, the current reference SIMD transcoder; pick utf8lut only for SSSE3-era x86 targets with BMP-heavy non-Latin text, or to study the LUT method. For grapheme, normalization or collation work (ICU, ICU4X, uni-algo, libutf, ugrapheme) it is not a substitute.
verified_claims_summary: The README's FileConverter run on a Ryzen 1600 (single core, 1 MB buffer converted RAM to RAM repeatedly, validating mode in both rows) measured the SSSE3 fast path at 1.65 vs 15.3 cycles/byte (random 1-3 byte code points, decode), 0.74 vs 9.9 (random, encode), 1.00 vs 9.10 (War and Peace fb2, decode) and 0.68 vs 4.89 (fb2, encode) against its own scalar path (Hoehrmann DFA decoder, branchy scalar encoder); the compiler is only implied as MSVC (/O2 /Oi), version not stated, and no incumbent such as ICU or iconv is in that table.
status_note: Abandoned since 2020 (migrated from Bitbucket, author calls it a proof of concept) but BSL-1.0 and about 20 source files with fuzz-style correctness tests, so it is easy to vendor or mine for the technique; for production pick a maintained SIMD transcoder with ASCII fast paths and runtime dispatch.
sources_read: WebSearch snippets for arXiv 2109.10433 (Lemire and Mula, Software: Practice and Experience 52(2), 2022); arxiv.org and r-libre.teluq.ca returned ENOTFOUND here
